newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire rebels preparing for army counter-attack.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels preparing for army counter-attack.

text.p: The leader of the rebels who defeated Zaire's ragged army in the country's east said on Tuesday he was ready to hold talks but that government troops were planning to attack with the aid of mercenaries.

"We are not attacking and we are asking for negotiations, but they don't want to negotiate so we will be forced to defend ourselves," said Laurent Kabila, head of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL).
"We expect them to attack soon, maybe within days, they are preparing a very big movement," Kabila told Reuters in Goma.
The French Le Monde newspaper on Tuesday reported several hundred European and African mercenaries were assembling in eastern Zaire to help stem advances by the Rwanda-backed rebels.

The daily said the force numbers between 200 and 300 and was expected to grow rapidly when more men leave Europe in two weeks to join South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican soldiers of fortune on the spot.
Mobutu Sese Seko has ruled out negotiations with Kabila and has instead promised a "devastating counter-offensive".

Kabila said Mobutu's army, with help from French troops and Hutu soldiers of the former Rwandan army -- defeated in 1994 by Rwandan Tutsi rebels who took over the government -- had started sending long range patrols out of Kisangani, 600 km (400 miles) northwest of Goma.

French officials had denied that report, saying the only French military on Zairean soil was a handful of gendarmes guarding the French embassy in Kinshasa and the military attache in the same mission.

With Zaire facing its worst crisis in decades Mobutu, who recently returned from Europe where he was treated for prostate cancer, has promised to do everything in his power to drive the rebels out of the vast mineral-rich central African state.
In three months Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces has overrun a 600 km (400 miles) strip of eastern Zaire along the border with Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi.

But the rebels have not yet been able to advance far into Zaire itself and the furthest positions which have been independently confirmed as under rebel control are at Walikale 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Goma.
Kabila said Mobutu's troops were now equipped with four Mirage jets as well as tanks and armoured cars.
"Soldiers of the former Rwandan army together with the Special Presidential Division (DSP) are trying to discipline the other units of the army and get them to fight," Kabila said.

Le Monde said the mercenaries called their force the "White Legion" and some of its members were recruited by retired Colonel Alain Le Carro, head of the presidential guard at the Elysee palace during late president Francois Mitterrand's rule.

French Cooperation Minister Jacques Godfrain said there were mercenaries from some European nations in the region but denied any official French involvement, saying Paris was victim of a smear campaign in the media.
"There are mercenaries from European countries in the region and people are pointing the finger at us when we're doing nothing," he told Reuters at a reception in Paris.
France backs Mobutu politically but is officially prevented from giving him military help because of an international arms embargo on Zaire.
Africa's latest war was ignited by Zairean attempts to expel the Banyamulenge -- an ethnic Tutsi group -- back to Rwanda, a land they left up to 200 years ago.
